K4-L3B · Day 13 · Monitoring & LLMOps · Lê Đức Hùng · 2A202602849

Make an LLM app observable — then prove it on a real incident.

Starting from a chat-agent skeleton with a set of TODOs, I added structured logging with PII redaction, distributed tracing with prompt versioning, a six-panel dashboard with an SLO and alerts — and used them to trace a slow-retrieval incident from a metric all the way to a single span.

The goalThree signals, one request

The lab is about connecting the signals an on-call engineer actually has, so that an alert turns into a root cause in minutes, not guesses.

MetricsSomething is wrong, and when. (P95 latency, error rate, cost…)
→
LogsWhich request. JSON lines carrying a correlation_id.
→
TracesWhich step. Same correlation_id on the Langfuse trace.
→
Root causeFix now, prevent next time.

Diagnose

Correlation ID on every log line and every trace observation, so one request can be followed across systems.

Protect

PII (email, VN phone, CCCD, card) is redacted before anything is serialised or written — in logs and in traces.

Operate

Prompt versions with labels (rollback without deploying), token/cost tracking, an SLO with an error budget, and symptom-based alerts with runbooks.

What I builtCheckpoint by checkpoint

CP0 · Setup & honest baseline

Ran the untouched skeleton and recorded it: validate_logs.py 30/100, 22 tests, correlation IDs all MISSING. Kept a copy of that baseline so the improvement is measurable.

CP1 · Logging & PII

  • Middleware: accepts x-request-id only if req-<8 hex>, else generates one; clears context per request; returns x-request-id and x-response-time-ms.
  • Every log carries user_id_hash (never the raw id), session_id, feature, model, env.
  • A recursive scrubber runs before the JSON renderer and file writer.

CP2 · Traces, prompts, dashboard

  • Trace day13-agent-request → lab-agent-run → retrieval + generation (Langfuse SDK v4).
  • Generation records model, input/output tokens, cost and a link to the managed prompt version.
  • Agent input/output capture switched off so raw messages never reach Langfuse.
  • Six-panel dashboard rendered from data/logs.jsonl; SLO + three alerts + runbook.

CP3 · Official challenge

Ran inject_incident.py and load_test.py --challenge --concurrency 5 with the class-specific challenge file (kept out of git), then walked Metrics → Logs → Trace → Root cause → Fix → Prevention.

Prompt versioning — a real promote and rollback

StepProduction label →Trace (same input)
Beforev1 (baseline)6be6836d… (req-ab000203)
Promotev2 (candidate → production)b0857f31… (req-ab000204)
Rollbackv1 againbb45a4e9… (req-ab000205)

The app never changes: it asks Langfuse for label production; moving the label moves the traffic.

SLO, error budget, alerts

SLO: 99.5% of requests answered within 3000 ms over 28 days.
Error budget: 0.5% → out of 10,000 requests, at most 50 may be slow or failed.
Three symptom-based alerts (Slack #k4-l3b-alerts, owner, runbook each):
  • HighLatencyP95 — warning, > 2000 ms for 5 m
  • ElevatedErrorRate — critical, > 2% for 10 m
  • DegradedRetrievalSuccess — warning, < 90% for 15 m

The incidentFrom a metric to one span

Challenge day13-k4-l3b-monitoring-llmops-v1 · 2026-09-30 · five requests at concurrency 5.

StepWhat I found
1 MetricP95 latency ≈ 2665 ms vs ≈ 170 ms normally. TTFT (50 ms), error rate (0%) and retrieval success (100%) all normal → only latency moved.
2 Logresponse_sent correlation_id=req-583d7b8f, latency_ms=2660; all five challenge requests 2653–2665 ms.
3 TraceTrace b54dcfcd… has the same correlation ID: lab-agent-run 2.66 s = retrieval 2.50 s + generation 155 ms.
4 Root causeThe rag_slow incident makes retrieval sleep 2.5 s (~94% of request time).
5 Fixinject_incident.py --disable → latency back to ~160–320 ms.
6 PreventionIncident P95 (2665 ms) breached the challenge threshold (2000 ms) but not my 3000 ms SLO, so an alert at 3000 ms would have missed it. I lowered HighLatencyP95 to 2000 ms as an early-warning alert. Proposed next: retrieval timeout + fallback.

Decisions & limitsWhat I would say out loud

Key technical decision

Lower the latency alert to 2000 ms instead of trusting the SLO number: measurement showed the real incident would have slipped under the SLO threshold. The SLO and the dashboard contract stay as specified.

Blockers I hit

  • Traces first lacked tokens/cost, and were lost when I killed the API right after a request (spans not flushed).
  • uvicorn ignores .env without --env-file, so tracing was silently off.
  • Langfuse's legacy traces API returns 410 → use observations v2.
  • The class challenge file had been committed by mistake; I untracked it and restored the documented path.
Known limits (honest). Fetching the prompt from Langfuse has no span of its own, so a few cold-start requests (2.3–3.0 s) can't be explained by a span. The dashboard is a static page generated from the log, not a live tool. The challenge file still exists in the pushed git history (e71de5d); removing it needs a history rewrite.
Why it matters. The same pattern — correlation ID, redaction before write, versioned prompts, token/cost tracking, SLO-based alerts — is what turns a demo chatbot into something you can operate.
